why: Two separate things make a run's declared harness commit differ from the commit holding the runner it actually executed, and both are recorded here rather than by editing the manifests, which are measurement records.
authoritative_field: runner_sha256 - the sha256 of bench/retest_runner.py itself. The identity rewrite did not touch file contents, so it still resolves against this history. harness_tree_sha is what the caller declared, and the manifest labels it 'declared via BENCH_HARNESS_SHA'.

cause_1_identity_rewrite.what: On 2026-08-27 this branch's 114 commits were rewritten so all carry the repository's configured identity, 84045975+thc1006@users.noreply.github.com, instead of a second address GitHub showed as unlinked. The tree at HEAD is byte-identical before and after; 50 commit objects got new SHAs.

cause_2_driver_declared_the_wrong_commit.what: A driver script bakes BENCH_HARNESS_SHA in when it is written and the runner is read when it executes. Where the runner was updated in between - or where the script was edited while it waited for the GPU, so bash kept the already-parsed value - the declared commit is the one the script was written against, not the one holding the runner that ran.
